TL;DW Executive Summary:
This video breaks down compound annual growth rate (CAGR), one of the most important metrics in quantitative finance, by explaining how geometric compounding turns portfolio returns into long-term wealth creation
I highlighted that true investment growth is multiplicative rather than linear; by contrasting arithmetic growth with geometric growth, I showed how reinvested returns create convexity, producing

over time
I clarified that risky assets like stocks do not compound in a smooth straight line, but instead follow jagged, stochastic return paths; CAGR compresses that volatility into a single fixed annual rate that explains the same beginning and ending portfolio value
I used the S&P 500's historical inflation-adjusted CAGR of roughly 7.5% to demonstrate how long-term market returns can double capital approximately every 9.6 years under the Rule of 72, turning patience and discipline into exponential portfolio growth
Ultimately, I framed CAGR as both a powerful investing tool and a reality check, showing how it can evaluate long-term portfolio feasibility, expose unrealistic day-trading claims, and help investors understand the difference between historical performance, future uncertainty, and sustainable wealth-building

I hope you enjoyed, and I hope you learned something!

Roman
